name: TRINIDAD
lead: Trinidad and Tobago is a pair of islands. Trinidad lies 11 km off Venezuela, a South American country. It gave the world the steelpan, calypso songs, and a wild street party.

facts.label: High point
facts.sub: El Cerro del Aripo, N. Range

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Trinidad was once attached to South America. The Gulf of Paria between them is so shallow you could almost wade across.
Tobago lies 30 km northeast, with coral reefs, fishing villages, and jungle. Together the islands cover 5,131 km².
animals: The scarlet ibis is Trinidad's national bird. Thousands roost in Caroni Swamp and glow flamingo-red at sunset. The shrimps they eat make them red.
Tobago's bird is the cocrico, a noisy forest bird that wakes everyone at dawn. Both birds are on the coat of arms.
culture: Other carnivals copy Trinidad's Carnival, a costume party. Before Lent (the weeks before Easter), Port of Spain erupts in costumes and soca music. At J'ouvert, people cover themselves in paint and mud before sunrise.

The steelpan was born in the 1930s, when colonial rulers banned drumming. Young musicians hammered oil drums into tuned instruments. It is the only non-electric instrument invented in the 20th century.
history: The explorer Columbus landed in 1498 and named the island after three peaks. Spain, France, and Britain followed. Enslaved Africans worked sugar plantations until 1838, then workers from India arrived.
Oil was struck in 1857. Independence came on 31 August 1962, with Dr. Eric Williams as first Prime Minister. It became a republic (led by a president) in 1976.
wows: Pitch Lake, a lake of natural tar, holds 10 million tonnes. Explorer Raleigh sealed ships with it in 1595.
The steelpan, the only non-electric instrument invented in the 20th century, has its own UN day, 11 August.
Cricket star Brian Lara scored 400 runs without getting out in 2004, the highest Test innings ever.
Trinidad sits on South America's rock base, so it is not a volcanic island.
Pitch Lake heals its own cracks, and swallowed objects resurface decades later.
Over 470 bird species live here, more than all of Europe.
Doubles, curried chickpeas in fried bread called bara, were invented in the 1930s.

myths.fact: Trinidad lies south of the main hurricane belt. Big storms rarely reach it.
Carnival belongs to Trinidadians. It grew from the resistance of enslaved Africans.
